text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The chairman of Sweden's central bank and former Social Democratic Finance Minister Kjell-Olof Feldt called in an editorial for the minority Social Democratic government to take over responsibility for social welfare from municipalities as the government has set up detailed rules anyway.

- Swedish investment company Investor, the key holding company in the Wallenberg family's financial empire, has increased its stake in family bank S-E-Banken, possibly to pave the way for new merger discussions between the bank and rival Nordbanken. Investor has increased its stake to 6.5 percent of equity and votes and when including other Wallenberg shares in the bank, the family controls 20 percent of capital and votes. The banks' previous merger discussions failed.

- Investor's 1996 earnings were a disappointment. Although the profit after financial items rose more than three-fold to 9.60 billion crowns, the company would have posted a large loss without the capital gain from selling 55 percent of shares in Swedish truck maker Scania. In addition, Investor merely raised dividend by one crown a share to ten crowns, compared with expectations for a three crown increase. Therefore, the share dropped nine crowsn to 336 crowns.
- The Saab 9-5 model will at last give the company the distinct profile it needs in order to help Saab Automobile swing to profit.

- A stronger dollar -- which has increased 13 percent in the past four months against the crown -- and economic recovery in Europe will lift Swedish exports this year. The export council will raise its forecast for export as a result. The stronger Norwegian crown and the British pound will also help.
- It is possible to increase employment and hold inflation at a European level in Sweden, on condition that wage increases will not be too high, an economic report showed.
- Special tax control in the 1995 and 1996 gave state coffers five billion extra crowns.
- Christer Tullberg, head of Swedish package maker Tetra Pak in southern China, says there will be no power struggle after the death of China's Deng Xiaoping and that politics will not be affected.

- Investment company Investor, the key holding company in the Wallenberg family's financial empire, increased its stake in S-E-Banken by 17.5 million shares, raising its voting stake to six percent. Including other Wallenberg holdings, the family thereby controls 18.4 percent of the bank's votes.
- The Saab 9-5 model will save loss making U.S.-Swedish car maker Saab Automobile AB, the company hopes.
- There was no end to deflation as the experts had thought. Swedish consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in January for a year-on-year fall of 0.1 percent.
